Kuvitus: korkealla peltojen, metsien ja: Illustration: high above fields, forests and a lake, two skydivers. At the upper left a skydiver falls belly down with arms and legs spread, and lines of the airflow are seen above. At the lower right another skydiver floats slowly under an open parachute. At the top edge of the sky is the aeroplane they jumped from.
Kolme vaihetta laskuvarjohyppääjän pudot: Three stages of a skydiver's fall belly down, to scale. At the top are situation pictures and at the bottom free-body diagrams in which the skydiver is a rectangle. On the left, right after the jump: the skydiver starts from rest relative to the air, the speed is zero, the free-body diagram has only the weight G from the centre down, and the orange acceleration arrow points down. In the middle the skydiver accelerates: a blue velocity arrow down, the weight G down and the air resistance F_v from the bottom up to the bottom surface, half the length of the weight, and the acceleration arrow is shorter. On the right terminal velocity: a long velocity arrow down, the air resistance as long as the weight, and the acceleration is zero.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa, simulaation malli: Graph to scale, values of the simulation model: on the horizontal axis time 0 to 30 seconds, on the vertical axis speed 0 to 70 metres per second. A dashed straight line rises steeply: the speed without air resistance, 49 metres per second at five seconds. Two curves start with the same steepness but flatten and level off horizontally: the speed of the 60 kilogram skydiver at about 48 metres per second and of the 100 kilogram skydiver at about 61 metres per second.
Kaksi tilannetta, mittakaavassa: suoraan: Two situations, to scale: a ball thrown straight up, when air resistance is not ignored. At the top are situation pictures and at the bottom free-body diagrams in which the ball is a rectangle. On the left the ball rises: a blue velocity arrow up. In the free-body diagram the weight G from the centre down and the air resistance F_v from the top surface down. Separately a green hollow net force arrow down, longer than the weight, and an orange acceleration arrow down. On the right the ball falls back: a velocity arrow down. In the free-body diagram the weight down and the air resistance from the bottom surface up. The net force arrow down is shorter than the weight, and the acceleration arrow is shorter than on the left.
Kolme vaihetta, kun laskuvarjo avataan,: Three stages when the parachute is opened, forces to scale. At the top are situation pictures and at the bottom free-body diagrams of the skydiver, in which the skydiver with the parachute is a rectangle. On the left falling before the parachute is opened, at terminal velocity: a long blue velocity arrow down, the weight G from the centre down and the air resistance F_v from the bottom up to the bottom surface, equally long, acceleration zero. In the middle the parachute opens: the velocity arrow still points down, the air resistance starts from the top surface and points up and is three times the length of the weight. Separately a green hollow net force arrow up and an orange acceleration arrow up. On the right the parachute is open: a short velocity arrow down, the air resistance from the top surface up as long as the weight, acceleration zero.
Vasemmalla tilannekuva: hyppääjän laskuv: On the left a situation picture: the parachute of the skydiver is opening, and next to the skydiver a blue velocity arrow points down. On the right the free-body diagram of the skydiver, the skydiver with the parachute as a rectangle: the weight G from the centre down and the air resistance F_v from the top surface up, almost three times the length of the weight. Separately an orange acceleration arrow up. On the right a small arrow y down: the positive direction is down.
Vasemmalla tilannekuva: lentopallo nouse: On the left a situation picture: a volleyball rises straight up, and next to it a blue velocity arrow points up. On the right the free-body diagram of the ball, the ball as a rectangle: the weight G from the centre down and the air resistance F_v from the top surface down.

On the left a situation picture: a volleyball rises straight up, and next to it a blue velocity arrow points up. On the right the free-body diagram of the ball, the ball as a rectangle: the weight G from the centre down and the air resistance F_v from the bottom surface up.

On the left a situation picture: a volleyball rises straight up, and next to it a blue velocity arrow points up. On the right the free-body diagram of the ball, the ball as a rectangle: the weight G from the centre down, the air resistance F_v from the top surface down and in addition a force F from the top surface up.

On the left a situation picture: a volleyball rises straight up, and next to it a blue velocity arrow points up. On the right the free-body diagram of the ball, the ball as a rectangle: the weight G from the centre down. There are no other arrows.
Mallikuvio: pallo on heitetty suoraan al: Model diagram: a ball has been thrown straight down faster than its terminal velocity, and it slows down. The diagram has only the ball as a rectangle. From the centre the weight G down and from the bottom surface the air resistance F_v up, clearly longer than the weight. Separately a blue velocity arrow down and an orange acceleration arrow up.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: vaaka-akselilla a: Graph to scale: on the horizontal axis time 0 to 3.0 seconds at half-second intervals, on the vertical axis speed 0 to 16 metres per second at one-metre intervals. The speed of the falling ball grows from zero first steeply and then more and more gently, to about 14 metres per second. A tangent has been drawn to the point P of the curve, at the moment of about 1.0 seconds and the speed of about 8 metres per second. The tangent passes through the points (0 s; 2.0 m/s) and (2.0 s; 15.0 m/s).
